news.title: Former Man Utd star and World Cup winner joins Zinedine Zidane's new France set-up in shock selection
news.lede: FABIEN BARTHEZ has linked back up with old pal Zinedine Zidane after being handed a surprise role with France. The former Manchester United keeper, 55, has been named as Les Bleus’ new goalkeeping coach. France officially unveiled Zidane’s brand new backroom team on Thursday morning after he replaced Didier Deschamps in the top job. And Barthez is one of the standout names joining the Real Madrid legend as France look ahead to Euro 2028 in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

news.title: FIFA chief Infantino receives support from 6 Arab federations amid revolt over World Cup plan
news.lede: The heads of six Arab soccer federations expressed their “full support” and “confidence” in Gianni Infantino on Thursday as the embattled FIFA president fights to keep his job after his failed World Cup private investment plan. The backing came from 2030 World Cup co-host Morocco, Qatar, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon and Sudan, with four of the signatories being FIFA council members. “We, the undersigned leaders of our respective football associations, express our full support for Mr. Gianni Infantino, President of FIFA, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide,” the statement read.

news.title: Bayern Munich’s Manuel Neuer on ‘very bitter’ World Cup exit
news.lede: Retirement has been a topic hovering around Manuel Neuer lately. The legendary goalkeeper came out of international retirement for a last run with Germany this summer, which ended in heartbreak at the Men’s World Cup. And the upcoming Bayern Munich season may be his last. But the 40-year-old just can’t get enough of football so far — and that’s a good thing.

(Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) Infantino is fighting to save his job after a barrage of criticism for his aborted plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
